access_restriction.description: Access restriction for the backup vault. Default value is 'WITHIN_ORGANIZATION' if not provided during creation. Default value: "WITHIN_ORGANIZATION" Possible values: ["ACCESS_RESTRICTION_UNSPECIFIED", "WITHIN_PROJECT", "WITHIN_ORGANIZATION", "UNRESTRICTED", "WITHIN_ORG_BUT_UNRESTRICTED_FOR_BA"]
access_restriction.rationale: Access restriction has security impact because it can be enforced through a whitelist of approved restrictive values to limit exposure.

allow_missing.description: Allow idempotent deletion of backup vault. The request will still succeed in case the backup vault does not exist.
allow_missing.rationale: Idempotent delete behavior; not enforced by policy.

annotations.description:
Optional. User annotations. See https://google.aip.dev/128#annotations
Stores small amounts of arbitrary data. 

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: Annotations have no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

backup_minimum_enforced_retention_durati.description: Required. The default and minimum enforced retention for each backup within the backup vault. The enforced retention for each backup can be extended.
backup_minimum_enforced_retention_durati.rationale: Minimum enforced retention needs security policy because it can be enforced through a simple minimum or range-based rule to reduce early deletion risk.

backup_retention_inheritance.description: How a backup's enforced retention end time is inherited. Default value is 'INHERIT_VAULT_RETENTION' if not provided during creation. Possible values: ["BACKUP_RETENTION_INHERITANCE_UNSPECIFIED", "INHERIT_VAULT_RETENTION", "MATCH_BACKUP_EXPIRE_TIME"]
backup_retention_inheritance.rationale: Selects how a backup's enforced retention end time is inherited (inherit the vault retention vs. match the backup expiry). It is an enum picking a retention-inheritance mode rather than enabling/lengthening retention itself; the prevent-loss control already lives on the minimum-enforced-retention and retention-day fields, so a generic policy here adds no security gain.

backup_vault_id.description: Required. ID of the requesting object.
backup_vault_id.rationale: Backup vault ID is an identifier and does not have any security implications.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: Optional. The description of the BackupVault instance (2048 characters or less).
description.rationale: Description has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

effective_time.description: Optional. Time after which the BackupVault resource is locked.
effective_time.rationale: Effective time has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

force_delete.description:
If set, the following restrictions against deletion of the backup vault instance can be overridden:
   * deletion of a backup vault instance containing no backups, but still containing empty datasources.
   * deletion of a backup vault instance that is being referenced by an active backup plan.
force_delete.rationale: Forcing deletion of a backup vault can result in permanent loss of backup data, but it is deprecated

force_update.description:
If set, allow update to extend the minimum enforced retention for backup vault. This overrides
 the restriction against conflicting retention periods. This conflict may occur when the
 expiration schedule defined by the associated backup plan is shorter than the minimum
 retention set by the backup vault.
force_update.rationale: Force updates may override protective measures and result in unwanted changes to configuration or data.

ignore_backup_plan_references.description:
If set, the following restrictions against deletion of the backup vault instance can be overridden:
   * deletion of a backup vault instance that is being referenced by an active backup plan.
ignore_backup_plan_references.rationale: Deletion behavior option; not enforced by policy.

ignore_inactive_datasources.description:
If set, the following restrictions against deletion of the backup vault instance can be overridden:
   * deletion of a backup vault instance containing no backups, but still containing empty datasources.
ignore_inactive_datasources.rationale: Deletion behavior option; not enforced by policy.

labels.description:
Optional. Resource labels to represent user provided metadata. 

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels have no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

location.description: The GCP location for the backup vault.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project is an administrative scoping field used to determine where the resource is created. It does not directly define or enforce a generic explicit security control for the vault itself.

encryption_config.description: Encryption configuration for the backup vault.

encryption_config.kms_key_name.description: The Resource name of the Cloud KMS key to be used to encrypt new backups. The key must be in the same location as the backup vault. The key must be a Cloud KMS CryptoKey.
encryption_config.kms_key_name.rationale: KMS-based encryption has security impacts, although the exact key validation is usually organization-specific, but not writing a policy in T1/26
